analysis.title: Buying Into The Muse-Hype - Thoughts Into 3Q Earnings
key_insights: DB reiterates Buy and $820 price target on Meta, based on 27x 2027E earnings (up from 25x) to reflect strong adoption of the Muse agent.

3Q channel checks show core advertising remains strong on higher engagement and ROAS-driven CPM growth. DB raises 3Q consolidated revenue estimate to $63.7bn from $63.1bn, implying +25.4% y/y FXN growth.
The buyside is thought to be modestly above the 3Q revenue guide of $64bn, with the high end of the 4Q26 outlook expected near $74-74.5bn in consolidated revenue.

Muse, Meta's recently launched consumer agent, shows durable downloads and adoption. DB expects direct monetization to come as the platform scales, through subscriptions, a commerce take-rate, interchange spread and ads in Muse's Feed tab.
DB expects the stock to keep trading on Muse downloads, users, engagement and retention, plus new model launches, under a 'scale-then-monetize' approach.
Costs are a clear debate. DB argues much of the capacity expansion and current CapEx is directed at scaling products like Muse and so is not incremental.
Investor conversations point to FY27 expectations of $210-225bn Opex and $230-240bn CapEx. DB raises its FY27 Opex estimate to $210bn from $204bn and CapEx to $232bn from $214bn.

Meta may offer a 'business in a box' solution built on Muse for the >200mn SMBs on its platforms. Channel checks show savings from agentic customer service being shifted to demand generation, which translates into ad revenue.
Recent model launches (Muse Wonder Family) mean Meta increasingly screens as a frontier lab, which could open subscription and enterprise revenue.

Ad checks: one agency saw Meta's two-year growth stack finish about 200bps ahead of expectations. A second check showed y/y spend growth accelerating about 200bps through 3Q. A third showed acceleration from 2Q26 to 3Q on AI-based tools released in 1Q26. Street expects about 150bps of FX-neutral deceleration.
CPM growth accelerated about 350bps sequentially in 3Q after about 650bps in 2Q, helped by click-through and conversion, a richer Reels and Stories mix, and Audience Network gains.
DB projects 3Q advertising revenue growth of +24.8% y/y FXN, about 1pt of deceleration from 2Q26 on a roughly 3pt tougher comp.
Expected call topics: Muse monetization timeline, enterprise ambitions, the split of owned-and-operated vs third-party capacity in FY27, longer-term capital intensity and funding sources.

Muse downloads and DAUs are well ahead of other AI apps at launch, including Sora, but remain significantly behind ChatGPT. Time spent on Muse has surpassed Gemini and is approaching ChatGPT, though a mature agent may see lower usage time because it works without prompting.

market_movers.rationale: Core advertising strength and Muse agent adoption ahead of 3Q earnings. The multiple basis moves to 27x 2027E earnings from 25x.

sector_views.rationale: Agentic tools are expanding the pool of advertisers and shifting SMB cost savings into ad spend, which benefits digital platforms.

earnings_insights: Meta 3Q26 consolidated revenue estimate (DB) raised to $63.7bn from $63.1bn, +25.4% y/y FXN, vs company 3Q guide of $64bn (high-end outlook, per the report).
Meta 3Q26 advertising revenue growth estimate (DB) +24.8% y/y FXN, about 1pt decel vs 2Q26 on a roughly 3pt tougher comp.
Buyside expects 4Q26 consolidated revenue at the high end of guidance, roughly $74-74.5bn (investor conversations, not DB's estimate).

FY27 Opex: DB estimate $210bn (from $204bn) vs investor expectation of $210-225bn. FY27 CapEx: DB estimate $232bn (from $214bn) vs investor expectation of $230-240bn. Both are forecasts. Meta is expected to give directional FY27 guidance on the 3Q call, as it did at 3Q25.

trade_ideas.description: Long META ahead of 3Q earnings (Buy, $820 price target)
trade_ideas.rationale: Core ad momentum, Muse adoption and a likely start of a rich product cycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Cost debate over Opex and CapEx, and the timeline for Muse monetization.

risk_factors: Rising Opex and CapEx, and the debate over whether they are incremental to Muse scaling.
Funding sources for FY27 capital intensity.
Street expects about 150bps of FX-neutral ad deceleration, a gap that may close either way.
Usage time on a mature agent may settle below chatbot levels.
vol_and_positioning: Buyside expectations for 3Q sit modestly above the revenue guide, and investors expect FY27 Opex and CapEx guidance on the call. The stock is trading on Muse downloads, users, engagement and retention.

tension_points.bull_case: Much of the capacity expansion and current CapEx is directed at scaling products like Muse and so is not incremental. Muse is naturally monetizable through subscriptions, commerce take-rate, interchange spread and Feed ads. Core ads are accelerating.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors expect FY27 Opex of $210-225bn and CapEx of $230-240bn, and the cost of frontier model launches is a clear debate. Muse monetization is likely to lag the scale-up.
tension_points.what_invalidates: FY27 Opex and CapEx guidance on the 3Q call well above the $210-225bn and $230-240bn investor expectations, or no timeline for Muse monetization.

theme_stances.key_argument: Muse is seeing durable downloads and adoption, pointing to significant early demand for personal AI agents among US consumers.
